have to occur by an alternate mechanism, (e.g., cephalic phase responses).
Ace-K is almost completely absorbed through the small intestine and enters the circulation. Absorption efﬁciency is not deter-
mined by level of exposure. Ace-K is not metabolized and is cleared rapidly, primarily by the kidneys, and excreted in the urine.
However, low concentrations have also been detected in breast milk (Sylvetsky et al., 2015). Thus, this sweetener would theoreti-
cally have the capacity to serve as a ligand for peripheral sweet receptors.
Saccharin is largely (85%–95%) absorbed through the small intestine and enters the circulation. It is not metabolized and is
cleared rapidly, primarily by the kidneys, and excreted in the urine. However, low concentrations have also been detected in breast
milk (Sylvetsky et al., 2015). Thus, saccharin would have the capacity to serve as a ligand for peripheral sweet receptors. A small
fraction (5%–15%) of saccharin passes into the colon. However, given the very low concentration initially ingested (due to its
high potency as a sweetener) and efﬁcient absorption, its concentration in the colon is extremely low. Thus, it is unlikely it serves
as a meaningful substrate for the microbiota though a role in gut signaling is possible.
Sucralose is primarily (90–95%) undigested.
